title: The exercise-level injury filter fails open on untagged rows
documented_claim: Lists are screened against the injuries the user reported
actual_behavior: An exercise with no contraindication tags is declared not contraindicated and served. 360 of 1,887 rows carry no tag, so 19.1% of the catalogue cannot be withheld from anyone by any injury or movement restriction, on any surface
user_impact: An injured user is served movements that load the injured area, on a list the UI says was screened
health_safety_impact: Direct: the safety promise is unmet for a fifth of the catalogue
minimal_fix: Ship untagged rows behind an explicit unscreenable state yielding Degraded plus a per-list caveat, or exclude them from recommending surfaces
minimal_test: eligibleExercises([untaggedRow], kneeInjuryContext) returns Degraded or empty, not Allowed. Mutation: restore the early return false, test goes red

title: No pregnancy or postpartum path exists anywhere
documented_claim: The app screens the whole person before prescribing exercise
actual_behavior: Never asked, never inferred, never filtered, never warned. Two tests use pregnancy specifically as an INVALID value. cycle_phase.dart:56-64 records a deliberate decision not to hold a pregnancy status, which is defensible - but declining to store it is not declining to generate a plan
user_impact: A pregnant or early-postpartum user receives a full unmodified programme including loaded spinal flexion and supine work
minimal_fix: One self-reported question persisting only a boolean, routed to wholePersonBlocks with a referral - the shape SurgeryStatus.underRestrictions already uses. Holds no medical category
minimal_test: SafetyContext(pregnancy: yes).allowsAnyTraining == false and buildPlan returns PlanRefused

title: The questionnaire-built programme bypasses the whole-person safety gate
documented_claim: buildPlan and buildProgramme both refuse when !safety.allowsAnyTraining
actual_behavior: programmeSpecFor returns null for from_answers, shred_endurance and shoulders_arms, so enrolment falls through to buildProgrammeSchedule, which takes no SafetyContext argument at all. Its catalogue applies the injury filter only
user_impact: A user refused training by PAR-Q+, by clinician advice, or under post-operative restrictions can still enrol and receive 24 scheduled sessions written to storage
health_safety_impact: Direct: the refusal state the product built is skipped on its default path
minimal_fix: Hoist the allowsAnyTraining refusal above the spec branch and pass eligibleExercises into the fallback
minimal_test: Enrol from_answers with a screening-blocked profile; assert zero ScheduledSession rows and a stated refusal

title: The AI can invent an exercise and it reaches the user with no catalogue or safety validation
documented_claim: Exercise guidance comes from a curated catalogue
actual_behavior: parseDescription validates only is-a-string, non-empty, at most 120 chars, deduped, capped at 5. No catalogue check, no injury screen, no equipment check, no disclaimer on the card
user_impact: Free-text model output is presented as what the user can do on a machine, including to a user with a reported injury
health_safety_impact: The text never touches the eligibility layer
minimal_fix: Match uses against the catalogue or aliases and render only matched rows; otherwise render summary alone with an explicit not-from-our-library line
minimal_test: Stub CloudAsk returning an invented movement; assert the card renders no uses or flags them

title: The chest-pain block carries no urgent-evaluation message
documented_claim: PAR-Q+ blocking answers route the user to a professional
actual_behavior: A user reporting pain in the chest at rest gets the same routine wording as every other blocking answer, and on non-onboarding surfaces only No sessions right now
user_impact: A user with a cardiac symptom is given non-urgent phrasing
minimal_fix: Branch the refusal copy on kBlockingQuestions membership; chest pain gets urgent wording and a localisable emergency route
minimal_test: Widget test: verdict blocked by chestPain renders the urgent string, blocked by medicallySupervisedOnly does not

title: A safety claim sits above health fields that reach no filter

privacy_impact: Sensitive data collected under a false purpose

minimal_test: Assert step_health does not render a string claiming the fields keep the plan safe

actual_behavior: The badge ships on two screens; the counter-disclosure ships on neither. Six exercise-serving surfaces carry no disclosure at all

minimal_fix: Render SafetyDisclosure on every surface that serves an exercise list
minimal_test: Widget test per surface asserting the disclosure is present

title: The default programme path selects alphabetically adjacent exercises
documented_claim: programme_builder.dart:5-16 documents this defect as fixed
actual_behavior: _fillDay takes pool[startAt] and walks consecutive indices of an id-sorted pool. Every catalogue row is durationMinutes 10, so a 45-minute session is exactly four adjacent rows. Day 0 is two yoga poses, a sit-up and a plyometric jump, for any goal
user_impact: The one surface claiming to be built from the user answers is the least structured path in the app
minimal_fix: Add a ProgrammeSpec for the profile programme so the null branch is unreachable, then delete the fallback
minimal_test: Enrol with goal=strength; assert movementRoleOf covers at least 4 primary strength roles across a week

title: The fallback repeats three of four exercises between consecutive days
documented_claim: _fillDay never repeats within a day
actual_behavior: startAt is (week + slot) % pool.length, so day 0 and day 1 overlap by three. week+slot also collides across weeks, so eight weeks draw on a window of about ten exercises
user_impact: The same four movements on Monday, Wednesday and Friday under a programme that promised variety
minimal_fix: Use (week * slotsPerWeek + slot) * picked.length as the stride, or route everything through buildProgramme
minimal_test: Build a 3-day 4-week fallback programme; assert pairwise session id-set overlap at most 1

title: AI-generated exercises are excluded only for users with a logged injury, never for a movement restriction
documented_claim: Generated rows are withheld from users who need screening
actual_behavior: hasInjuries reads profile.health.injuries only. ai:: rows carry no contraindications, so a restriction-only profile passes and can resolve them
user_impact: A user who reported that overhead movement is limited can be taken into the player on an untaggable AI-authored exercise
minimal_fix: Widen the predicate to injuries.isNotEmpty || flags.restrictions.isNotEmpty
minimal_test: Resolve a cached ai:: id for a restrictions-only profile; assert notFound
